solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Manager plunged into Eastern sea showing relief

indicators.note: the manager is dropped right inside the sea, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Med, short for the Mediterranean Sea
a boss is a manager

explanation.surface: A boss takes a dip in an eastern sea and gets some relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relief' looks like comfort after a swim, but it is the raised design of embossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Embossed metal or paper carries a raised design, which is what relief means in art and printing.

clue.text: Use my pole when rambling

indicators.note: rambling suggests wandering about aimlessly, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes a walking pole out on a ramble.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a tool or method is to make use of it; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Pound — main place for stray dogs

parts.note: to pound something is to batter it
the main is an old poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: A dog pound is the chief place where stray dogs end up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' reads as the dogs' enclosure but is the verb to batter. Battersea Dogs and Cats Home in London is Britain's best-known rescue centre for strays.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is the London district famous for its dogs' home, a refuge for strays since Victorian times.

clue.text: Politician organised treason

indicators.note: organised implies arranging things differently, so the letters of treason are rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician has planned an act of treachery against the state.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, a legislator and therefore a politician.

clue.text: Elizabeth's favourite fearless explorer embraced

indicators.note: embraced means held within, so the answer sits inside the words fearless explorer

explanation.surface: Queen Elizabeth's favourite courtier was a bold explorer whom she took to her heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, was the favourite of Elizabeth I; the bold explorer of the surface makes Raleigh the tempting thought.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Essex was famously a court favourite of Queen Elizabeth I before his fall.

clue.text: Dish for alcoholic drink

definitions.meaning: to dish hopes or plans is to ruin them, to put a stop to them

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a serving dish to hold a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour is to quash it, as to dish a chance is to wreck it; Scotland's whisky bears the same name.

clue.text: Saving Trades Union Congress apparently

definitions.meaning: an economy, a reduction in what is spent
a whimsical second reading: the union body's three initials, if a verb meaning slash is written in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A trade union body is apparently economising.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful cryptic reading: take the verb for slash, write it back to front, and you have the initials of Britain's Trades Union Congress; 'apparently' admits the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutback is a reduction in spending, a saving made by spending less.

clue.text: Time to get around for hidden treasure

parts.note: to rove is to wander or get around

explanation.surface: It is time to travel about in search of buried treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a store of valuable things found, as in treasure trove, buried riches discovered.

clue.text: The Queen embracing Murray, an all-round performer

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the Queen's letters wrap around the name

parts.note: HM stands for Her Majesty
Andy Murray, the British tennis champion

explanation.surface: The Queen hugs Andy Murray, a superb all-round sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Murray is the Scottish tennis player who won Wimbledon.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman can turn a hand to all sorts of jobs, a versatile all-round worker.

clue.text: Avid reader of Bellow getting over work being rewritten

indicators.note: the bellow stretches over and around the reworked letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a boom is a deep loud roar, a bellow

indicators.note: rewritten means set down again in a new form, so the letters of work are reordered

explanation.surface: A keen reader of the novelist Saul Bellow is going over a work being redrafted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bellow' looks like the American novelist Saul Bellow but is a deep roar; 'getting over' has that roar enclose the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookworm is someone who reads voraciously, an eager devotee of books.

clue.text: Move fast to suppress dissent

definitions.meaning: pressing the accelerator pedal to the floor in a car
to be firm and refuse to tolerate opposition

explanation.surface: Someone acts quickly to crush opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means pressing hard on the accelerator, and also taking a firm stand against disobedience.

clue.text: Work too hard to get public a vote

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
an X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Someone toils excessively to win a public vote.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtax something is to strain it beyond its capacity, to push it too hard.

clue.text: King rejected an extremely wicked activity

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: rejected suggests being sent back, so the little word an is turned around

parts.note: very means extremely

explanation.surface: A king has turned down something exceedingly wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Knavery is roguish dishonesty, the conduct of a knave or scoundrel.

clue.text: English journalists gripped by such strong drink

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside, so the journalists sit within the word for such

parts.note: so can mean such, as in 'so it is'
the press is the body of journalists

explanation.surface: English reporters are hooked on a powerful drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An espresso is a small, intense shot of coffee, a strong drink without alcohol.

clue.text: Small publication promoting revolution

parts.note: an edition is an issue of a book or newspaper

explanation.surface: A little magazine is stirring up revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is speech or action that incites rebellion against the state's authority.

clue.text: Knight — alias covering fine author

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the alias encloses the letter for fine

parts.note: aka is short for also known as
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A knight using an assumed name conceals a fine writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Kafka was the Prague-born author of The Trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Kafka was a twentieth-century novelist and short-story writer.

clue.text: Footwear for beach somersault is a failure

parts.note: a flip is a somersault in the air
a show that flops is a failure

explanation.surface: Turning a somersault on the beach turns out to be a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Flip-flops are light thonged sandals worn at the seaside.

clue.text: He helped make mummy glower when accepting endless charity

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the shortened word goes inside the glowing coal

parts.note: an ember is a thing that glows, read as glow-er

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: Mum glares at someone when she is offered unending charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' reads as a scowl but means something that glows, an EMBER. 'Mummy' is not a mother but an Egyptian preserved body.
explanation.definitionFit: An embalmer preserves a corpse, the work that produced Egyptian mummies.

clue.text: London police arresting a knight on purpose

indicators.note: the police hold the other pieces inside, as they hold someone they arrest

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: London's police seize a knight deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meant was intended, done deliberately rather than by accident.

clue.text: Group of three making small journey?

definitions.meaning: a set of three, as in a poetic stanza or musical figure
a trip with the diminutive ending -let, read as a little trip

explanation.surface: Three companions set off on a short outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is a set of three things; jokingly, a trip made small by the suffix -let.

clue.text: Various items held by doctor in the house

indicators.note: held by means contained within, so the reordered letters go inside the doctor
various suggests different forms, so the letters of items are shuffled

explanation.surface: A doctor keeps assorted belongings at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic means relating to the home or household.

clue.text: Have evening meal traditionally including fish for a change

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the meal word wraps around the fish

parts.note: to sup is an old-fashioned word for eating supper
hake is a fish

explanation.surface: Diners have fish at supper by way of variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A shake-up is a radical reorganisation, a big change.

clue.text: Vulnerable bid

definitions.meaning: sore or easily hurt, as a bruise is
a formal offer, as made for a contract

explanation.surface: A weak offer is put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender flesh is sensitive and easily hurt; a tender is also an offer submitted for a contract.

clue.text: Give job to petty officer splitting a beer

indicators.note: splitting means breaking apart, so the officer goes into the middle of the beer

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer
PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer

explanation.surface: A naval officer is sharing a pint with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to assign them to a post, to give them a job.

clue.text: Ride bike round bend finally, ring bell

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the ringing wraps around the letter

parts.note: a peal is the ringing of bells

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of bend

explanation.surface: A cyclist rings the bell going round a bend.
explanation.definitionFit: To pedal is to work a bicycle's pedals, to ride it.

clue.text: Get hold of backward-looking people who like fairies

indicators.note: backward-looking means facing the other way, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: elf fans are devotees of fairy folk

explanation.surface: Fairy lovers are a nostalgic, old-fashioned bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are ELF FANS, people keen on fairies, read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To snaffle something is to grab or take it, often sneakily.

clue.text: Fight aquatic creatures coming up leaving river

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so the river's letter departs
coming up in a down entry means the word reads upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: otters are aquatic mammals
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Otters surface from a river and start scrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming up' turns OTTERS into SRETTO; taking out R leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief fight or argument.

clue.text: Here you'll find White Stripes music that's rather bland

definitions.meaning: the white lines painted along the centre of a road

explanation.surface: The rock band the White Stripes play music some find bland.
explanation.walkthrough: The White Stripes were an American rock duo, but here they are painted road markings.
explanation.definitionFit: Centre lines are painted down a road's midline, and moderate, inoffensive music is labelled with the same phrase.

clue.text: Tell of churchman losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a prelate is a senior churchman such as a bishop

explanation.surface: Someone recounts the tale of a clergyman being beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or narrate it.

clue.text: Bliss perhaps as Clegg's friend's meeting the Queen

parts.note: Compo is Clegg's friend in the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine; the 's stands for is, giving S
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Bliss is had when a friend meets the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Arthur Bliss was an English composer, Master of the Queen's Music. Last of the Summer Wine is a long-running British TV comedy in which Compo and Clegg are friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Bliss wrote orchestral and film music, an example of a composer.
